items.statement: Let (Ω,Σ,μ) be a probability space, let I be a finite nonempty index set, and let X:Ω→Mat_I(ℝ). Give real matrices the Euclidean operator-norm topology and use the Bochner integral and matrix-algebra power-series exponential. Suppose X is almost-everywhere strongly measurable, X and the ordinary matrix square X² are integrable, X=Xᵀ almost everywhere, I−X is positive semidefinite almost everywhere, and ∫X dμ=0. Then for every real s>0, exp((exp(s)−s−1)∫X² dμ)−∫exp(sX) dμ is positive semidefinite. The explicit regularity hypotheses expand Tropp§2.2 standing expectations. The claim is the real normalized individual-matrix form of Lemma6.7.
assumptions: Public scope: a probability space \((\Omega,\Sigma,\mu)\), a finite nonempty index set \(\mathcal I\), and a real random square matrix \(X:\Omega\to\operatorname{Mat}_{\mathcal I}(\mathbb R)\). The integral is Bochner integration and \(e^A\) is the matrix-algebra power series. The order \(U\preceq V\) means that \(V-U\) is positive semidefinite as a full quadratic form.

Public hypotheses: \(X=X^\top\) and \(X\preceq I\) almost surely, \(\int X\,d\mu=0\), and \(s>0\). The cap is one-sided. The matrix need not be positive semidefinite and negative eigenvalues are unrestricted.

Explicit source-standing regularity: \(X\) is almost-everywhere strongly measurable, \(\int\|X\|\,d\mu<\infty\), and \(\int\|X^2\|\,d\mu<\infty\). These are the sealed expansion of Tropp§2.2 sufficiently-regular expectation conventions; the preproof target/binder/topology admission accepted that expansion. The exponential integrability needed in the proof is derived from the cap.

\(X^2=X\cdot X\) is the ordinary matrix square. The exponent uses its actual matrix expectation \(\int X^2\,d\mu\), with coefficient \(e^s-s-1\). No scalar variance proxy or matrix covariance upper cover replaces that expectation.

obligations.label: The normalized real individual-MGF assertion of Tropp Lemma6.7.

bindings.boundary: The public node proves the complete real normalized individual-matrix MGF inequality. The associated private theorem proves its literal original-Gaussian specialization for the fixed weight w_i=+cos((2q+1)θ_i), including the negative values of that cosine. It supplies no separate public node. A global −cos specialization and a complete two-sided or matrix-sum tail are outside this packet. No Lieb/master-tail, full matrix Bernstein, FactC6, Lemma4.4, main lower bounds, oracle/TV/precision, query-cap/cost, production-site integration, purification or whole-Goal completion is established here. The original shared stabilization owner retains ownership.
